root_motivation: Grounding (truth-tier failures 2026-09-28/09-29; chain.rs:28-31,188,185-245; mod.rs:1181,1187; runs.rs:185-215). A chain publishes input_schema: {"type":"object"} -- it never says which $.input.<name> values its steps need, so the first call is args:{} and dies at step 1 with compose_mapping_missing (4 of 4 chain sessions, 09-28/09-29). A chain run leaves no per-step run rows: chain.rs's result carries a steps trace as the only stand-in, so 'did all three steps finish?' is unanswerable via host.runs.*, and the gold runs.last(tool=daily_pipeline).children.count == 3 can never be observed. Fix: derive required inputs from $.input.* mapping paths at publish time, refuse a call missing them before any step runs (compose_input_missing naming every missing field), and record one child run row per executed step (trigger: "composition", parent_run_id) that host.runs.get inlines one level deep.
user_persona: Two (PRD user stories): (1) a data-pipeline builder / workflow orchestrator agent that publishes a chain, learns its inputs from host.tool_spec/tools/list, and reads three done child runs after one call; (2) a SaaS operator running a per-end-user pipeline, who needs child runs to carry the parent's end_user_subject so per-user credential resolution and audit stay correct.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a chain published with steps [{fetch_data, args:{url:"$.input.url"}}, {transform, args:{rows:"$.prev.result.rows"}}, {write, args:{rows:"$.prev.result.rows", region:"$.input.region"}}], When tools/list is read, Then input_schema.required == ["url","region"].
Given a chain with no $.input.* paths, When published, Then its input_schema is exactly {"type":"object"}.

Given the chain from AC-1, When host.tool_call(name, args={}) is called, Then it fails compose_input_missing with data.missing == ["url","region"], data.step == 1, and host.runs.list(include_children=true) shows zero trigger="composition" rows for this tenant.

Given the chain from AC-1 and args {url, region}, When called and awaited, Then host.runs.get(parent).children has exactly 3 rows in step order, each with trigger == "composition", parent_run_id == parent, status == "done", tool equal to the step's tool.
Given that same run, When host.runs.list() is called with no filters, Then only the parent row appears; parent_run_id=parent shows exactly the 3 children; trigger="composition" shows the 3 children.

Given a 3-step chain whose step 2 fails with on_error: "stop", When awaited, Then the parent's outcome is a failure, child 1 is done, child 2 is failed with the step's error_class, and no child 3 row exists.
Given a 3-step chain run by an end user with end_user_subject = "alice", When children are read, Then each child's end_user equals the parent's.
Given one 3-step chain run, When host.usage and the calls ledger are read, Then the chain counts as exactly 1 call and the busyaudit/metering suites pass unchanged.

Given a tenant with one parent and 3 children, When admin tenant delete runs, Then all 4 run rows are gone; and when host.runs.purge covers the parent's window, the children's stored results are purged too.
Given host.tool_test on the chain from AC-1, When called, Then the report includes inputs_required == ["url","region"].
Given a failed child row, When host.runs.list(status="failed", trigger="composition") is read, Then the row carries step_no and parent_tool.
Given two chain runs and one compose_input_missing refusal, When /healthz is read, Then runs.composition_children_total == 6 and runs.composition_parents_failed_input_total == 1.

scope: src/kinds/chain.rs: derive input_schema.required from every step's $.input.<name> mapping path (describe()); host.tool_test's dry run also reports inputs_required; ChainKind::call refuses compose_input_missing before step 1 dispatches when a required input is missing from the call's args; ChainKind::validates_own_args() -> true so the generic dispatch-time schema validator (which would otherwise enforce the same input_schema.required BEFORE chain's own call() ever ran) steps aside.

src/kinds/mod.rs: Kind::validates_own_args() new trait method (default false); CallCtx::parent_run_id: Option<String> new field; compose_call gains a step_no: Option<i64> parameter and, when ctx.parent_run_id is Some, records one composed child run row (trigger: "composition") per dispatch attempt via Db::insert_composed_run, whatever the outcome (self-call refusal, depth/children ceiling, tool lookup, or the target Kind::call's own Ok/Err) -- 'one row per executed step' matches chain.rs's own pre-existing steps trace, which already reports a dispatch refusal the same way it reports the target's own failure.

src/db.rs: RunRow/RUN_COLUMNS gain parent_run_id/step_no/parent_tool (migration 0061, additive); Db::insert_composed_run, Db::get_run_children; Db::list_runs gains parent_run_id/include_children (default excludes composed children unless parent_run_id, trigger="composition", or include_children=true is given); Db::record_call_attributed_with_end_user gains an Option<String> pre-generated run_id parameter; Db::count_composition_children_total/count_composition_parents_failed_input_total for /healthz.

src/handler.rs: call_published_tool pre-generates its own run id BEFORE dispatch (was: generated only after the call returned) and threads it into CallCtx::parent_run_id so a composing chain's children can attribute to the not-yet-written parent row; host.tool_test/host.tool_call/host.tool_run/runs::enqueue[_shared]/compose_call all gain a `!kind.validates_own_args()` guard around the generic input_schema validator.

src/runs.rs: execute_job's CallCtx carries parent_run_id: Some(run.id) so an async/scheduled chain job gets the same lineage a synchronous call gets; runs::get inlines a run's direct children (one level, via get_run_children); runs::list parses parent_run_id/include_children.
src/http.rs: /healthz gains a runs: {composition_children_total, composition_parents_failed_input_total} block.
non_goals: No workflow engine: no branching, map steps, retries, or fan-out -- depth/children ceilings (COMPOSE_DEPTH_MAX, COMPOSE_CHILDREN_MAX) unchanged.
No recursion in `children` beyond one level -- a nested chain's own children are read by querying that child's run id directly, not auto-expanded.
No change to the $. mapping grammar; `outputs` promotion stays deferred as chain.rs already documents.

host.export archiving children under the parent's run id, and host.runs.cancel explicitly cascading to not-yet-started children (P0 requirement 7's other two clauses) -- not exercised by any listed AC; export's existing top-level-only scope is preserved unchanged rather than extended speculatively.
host.tool_test accepting args and reporting per-step mapping resolution against them (P2 requirement 10) -- no listed AC needs it beyond the existing dry-run/inputs_required behavior.
AC13 (the live truth-tier recipe score) -- operator-provisioned, deferred.

additional.chain_kind_generic_arg_validation_bypass: chain's new input_schema.required, if enforced by the SAME generic dispatch-time jsonschema validator every other kind uses (call_published_tool, host.tool_test, host.tool_run, compose_call, runs::enqueue[_shared]), would reject a call missing an input with args_invalid BEFORE chain's own Kind::call ever ran -- making compose_input_missing (AC3, naming every missing field) unreachable, and breaking host.tool_test's dry run on an incomplete call (AC10). Kind::validates_own_args() is the opt-out: true only for chain, every other kind unaffected.
additional.composed_child_rows_cover_every_dispatch: compose_call records a run row for EVERY dispatch attempt once lineage is active (ctx.parent_run_id is Some) -- including a self-call/depth/children-ceiling refusal or a tool-not-found lookup miss, not only a case where the target Kind::call itself ran -- matching chain.rs's own pre-existing steps trace, which already reports those same refusals as a step's own status/error_class (see tests/compose_ac7_on_error_continue.rs's 'step2 is deliberately never published' convention).

five_whys_trace.a: Gold children.count == 3 is False (no children in any run row) and, before that, the first run of the chain fails.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did the first run fail?
five_whys_trace.a: The agent called with args: {}; step 1 needed $.input.url.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did the agent pass nothing?
five_whys_trace.a: The published chain's input_schema is an empty object schema; host.tool_spec/tools/list show no required inputs, and host.tool_test's dry run reports the steps but not the inputs they will need.
The chain kind was scaffolded with mapping parsing for validation only; deriving a schema from $.input.* paths was not in that tick's scope, and no test asserted a chain's schema.

Explicitly deferred to a runs-and-jobs PRD that had not landed when chain.rs was scaffolded; the parent's own steps trace was accepted as a stand-in, and nothing downstream forced the issue until the truth-tier gold asked for lineage. Deepest actionable level: (a) publish-time input derivation + call-time pre-check; (b) child run rows written by compose_call for every step dispatch, inlined by host.runs.get.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC4/AC13 say 'run via host.tool_run' -- is that the literal host.tool_run RPC (a debug dispatch to Kind::tool_run, which chain never overrides, so it always returns tool_run_unsupported)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- Technical Considerations explicitly names the synchronous host.tool_call dispatch site (handler.rs::call_published_tool) as where CallCtx::parent_run_id is set, and the PRD's own evidence section's transcripts all use host_tool_call. Read 'run via host.tool_run' as generic phrasing for 'run it' (host.tool_call), not the distinct host.tool_run debug RPC.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC6 says 'the parent is failed' -- is that the literal run status string "failed"?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- this crate's existing call/job run status vocabulary is done/error/timeout/cancelled (no "failed"); only requirement 4's own text introduces done/failed as the CHILD status vocabulary specifically. The parent (written by the pre-existing generic call/job finalize path) keeps status "error" for a failure; 'the parent is failed' reads as a description of outcome, not a literal value, since AC6's own parallel wording for children ('child 2 is failed') does use requirement 4's literal new vocabulary.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should a composed child row exist for a step compose_call refuses BEFORE ever reaching the target's own Kind::call (self-call, depth/children ceiling, tool-not-found, schema mismatch)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes -- matches chain.rs's own pre-existing steps trace, which already reports exactly these refusals as a step's status/error_class (tests/compose_ac7_on_error_continue.rs relies on step2 never being published so its dispatch fails tool_not_found, asserted as steps[1].status == "error"). Treating every compose_call invocation (not just a successful hand-off into the target's own call) as 'one executed step' keeps the new run-row ledger and the pre-existing trace in agreement.
